decision: Adopt the OSS mask-indexed post-stream bounce-back (vivsim obstacle_bounce_back) as an *equivalent* solid closure for TensorLBM and replace the dense torch.where swap by a precomputed index-pair form (O(Q*N_solid)) where a geometry is static; keep the interpolated bounce-back for non grid-aligned (curved) walls. The decision is supported if and only if the semantic-identity gate and the physics gate below both pass.

oss_reference.execution_limit: vivsim is JAX; this environment has no jax (ModuleNotFoundError) and no GPU, so the OSS arm is a *literal transplant* of the cited one-liner into torch (boolean-mask select + scatter, same simultaneity), not an execution of the OSS binary. Recorded as a comparison limit, never upgraded silently.

alternatives.A1_oss_boolean: literal OSS rule: clone + f[:, mask] = f[opp][:, mask]  (cost O(Q*N_total))
alternatives.A2_mask_indexed: TensorLBM new operator: precomputed flat (dst,src) index pair over the solid cells; in-place variant costs O(Q*N_solid)
alternatives.A4_fluid_side: independently written fluid-side half-way bounce-back (out[i](x)=f_pre[i](x-c_i) if x-c_i fluid else f_pre[opp i](x))
alternatives.C1_interpolated: tensorlbm.boundary.interpolated_bounce_back (2-point Bouzidi, sub-grid q from an analytic SDF) - the curved-wall alternative

hypotheses.statement: A2 is bit-identical to A1 and to A3 on arbitrary fields and masks (2-D and 3-D, incl. masks touching the domain border and degenerate masks).
hypotheses.threshold: == 0.0 (bitwise; a representation change must be exact)

hypotheses.statement: The solid-node post-stream swap is exactly the fluid-side half-way bounce-back for the unforced BGK step; with a Guo body force the two agree only to the size of the forcing term.
hypotheses.metric: max |A2 - A4|_inf on a body-force channel after 1500 steps, run twice (g=0 and g=1e-5)
hypotheses.threshold: g=0: == 0.0 (bitwise); g>0: <= 1e-4 absolute on populations of order 0.1 (deviation is reported, not tuned)

hypotheses.statement: The closure is the half-way wall: plane-channel permeability equals the analytic k = H^2/12 with H = number of fluid rows (wall mid-planes), and it is second-order consistent in H.
hypotheses.threshold: |err| < 15% (owner band) at every H, and |err| < 1% for H >= 16; monotone decrease of |err| with H is reported but NOT required to pass (the previous verified case showed non-monotone behaviour and it is kept visible)

hypotheses.statement: Ignoring the half-way offset (using H = ny, i.e. counting the two solid wall rows as fluid) is a geometric bias that grows as 1/H and exceeds the owner band at coarse resolution.
hypotheses.metric: err_pct_if_H_eq_ny at the same H sweep
hypotheses.threshold: reported as a trap; predicted |err| ~ (ny/H)^2 - 1 -> 12% at H=8, 3% at H=32 (checked, not tuned)

hypotheses.statement: The index-pair form removes the per-step whole-domain gather: its per-application cost scales with the solid count, not with N_total, so the in-place index form beats the dense where swap whenever the solid fraction is small.
hypotheses.metric: wall time per application on a 512x512 float64 field, solid fraction in {0.005,0.02,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50}
hypotheses.threshold: speedup >= 1.5x vs dense where at solid fraction <= 0.10; speedup is reported for all fractions (both crossings reported)

hypotheses.statement: For a non grid-aligned (curved) wall the mask-indexed closure keeps the staircase surface, so on Schaefer-Turek 2D-1 (Re=20) its Cd error exceeds the interpolated (Bouzidi) closure's at the same resolution.
hypotheses.metric: |err Cd| (%) for D in {16, 24} against the in-repo anchor ref_cd = 5.57953523384 (benchmarks/verified/cylinder/re20_st/result.json)
hypotheses.threshold: owner band 15% applies to each arm; the *comparison* is reported as the adoption trade-off (no threshold invented to force a winner)

baselines.physics_baseline: analytic plane Poiseuille k = H^2/12 (wall mid-planes, H = fluid rows) and the analytic parabolic profile through the same wall positions
baselines.case_baseline: Schaefer-Turek 2D-1 Re=20 in-repo verified anchor Cd = 5.57953523384 (FeatFlow/Nabh spectral, result.json:ref_source)
baselines.representation_control: A1 / A2 / A3 / A4 integrate the same collision (BGK), the same Guo forcing, the same streaming and the same steady-state criterion - the closure is the only changed variable

stability_and_exclusions.stability_rule: a run producing a non-finite population, rho outside [0.95,1.05] or Ma > 0.1 is declared failed and reported, never tuned away
stability_and_exclusions.exclusions: none; no outlier removal, no post-hoc threshold change

stopping_rule: step counts are fixed before the run (channel 20000, ST2D1 12000 for D=16/24); a block may be stopped early only if wall clock exceeds 900 s, and any stopped block is reported as incomplete rather than silently dropped

changed: solid closure (A1/A2/A3/A4 for the identity+channel blocks; A2 vs C1 for the curved-wall block)
resolution H in {8,16,32,64} (channel) and D in {16,24} (ST2D1)
body force g x1 and x2 at H=32 (linearity of k)
solid fraction in {0.005,0.02,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50} for the cost block
held_fixed: D2Q9, BGK/SRT, float64, single CPU thread
Guo (2002) forcing, same formula in every arm
channel: nx=6, periodic in x, body force in x; ST2D1: Zou-He inlet profile + Zou-He outlet, geometry identical to the in-repo verified case
confounders: the OSS arm is a transplant (no jax), so runtime numbers are torch-vs-torch and cannot be compared with vivsim's JAX timings
torch where/index_copy kernel launch overhead dominates at small grids; the cost block uses one large grid to make the slope visible
the ST2D1 Cd also carries the Ladd momentum-exchange surface-force error on the staircase (in-repo note: MEM Cl is not convergent), so the curved-wall comparison is about Cd only

analysis: grouped by arm; per-KPI relative error to the analytic/anchor value; resolution and parameter sensitivities reported as separate tables; convergence claimed only from the measured sequences, never extrapolated
